title: Genomic ctDNA-Informed De-escalation And Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Omission in Cystectomy
official: GUIDANCE-MIBC: Genomic ctDNA-Informed De-escalation And Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Omission in Cystectomy
summary: This study is for participants who have recently been diagnosed with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are eligible for the surgical removal of the entire bladder, and have undergone ctDNA testing with a negative result. The purpose of this study is to investigate the outcomes for ctDNA negative MIBC participants who do not receive neoadjuvant chemotherapy before undergoing bladder removal.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Histologically confirmed muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder (cT2- T4aN0M0).
* Planned for radical cystectomy with curative intent.
* Negative for ctDNA using a validated, tumor-informed assay (Natera Signatera) from a blood sample collected prior to any systemic therapy. Must have 2 negative tests within the screening window.
* Age ≥ 18 years.
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 0, 1, or 2.
* Adequate organ function as defined by standard laboratory criteria.
* Ability to understand and provide written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Evidence of clinical node-positive or metastatic disease (cN+ or cM1) on baseline imaging.
* Prior systemic therapy (chemotherapy or immunotherapy) for urothelial carcinoma within the past 12 months.
* Positive ctDNA status at baseline (defined as a positive result on either of the two pre-operative Natera Signatera tests).
* Variant histology comprising \>50% of the tumor volume (e.g., small cell, sarcomatoid, plasmacytoid).
* Uncontrolled concurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, or psychiatric illness that would limit compliance with study requirements.
